questions.q: What is a slowly changing dimension?
options: A dimension table whose attribute values change occasionally rather than on every load, requiring a decision about whether to overwrite or preserve history
A fact table that loads very slowly due to poor indexing
A dimension table that never changes once created
A temporary staging table used only during a package's execution
questions.explain: Slowly changing dimensions are dimension tables where attributes change occasionally — like a customer's city or a product's category — and the warehouse must decide how to handle that change.

questions.q: What happens to a column configured as a Changing attribute when its incoming value differs from the stored value?
options: The old value is overwritten with the new one, with no history kept (Type 1 behavior)
The row is rejected as an error
A new dimension record is inserted and the old one is marked expired
Nothing — Changing attributes are never updated
questions.explain: Changing attribute is the classic Type 1 SCD behavior — overwrite in place, no history retained.

questions.q: What happens to a column configured as a Historical attribute when its value changes?
options: The old record is marked expired and a new record is inserted with the new value, preserving history (Type 2 behavior)
The value is silently discarded
The package throws a fatal error and stops
The old value is overwritten in place, same as a Changing attribute
questions.explain: Historical attribute is Type 2 behavior — the wizard inserts a new current record and expires the old one so history is preserved and queryable.

questions.q: What is an inferred member, and why does it exist?
options: A minimal placeholder dimension record created when a fact row references a dimension key that doesn't exist yet, later updated once real data arrives
A dimension record that was manually typed in by an administrator
A row that fails validation and gets logged to an error table
A backup copy of every dimension record, refreshed nightly
questions.explain: Inferred members let a fact load proceed even when the matching dimension data hasn't arrived yet — a placeholder record holds the key until real details show up.

questions.q: According to the Slowly Changing Dimension Wizard's generated data flow, what does the Historical Attribute Inserts Output feed into before reaching an OLE DB Command?
options: A Derived Column, which stamps expiration values before the insert/update logic runs
Directly into the OLE DB Destination with no further processing
A Conditional Split that routes it back to the source
A Sort transformation to reorder the rows
questions.explain: The wizard-generated flow runs the Historical Attribute Inserts Output through a Derived Column to set expiration-related values before its OLE DB Command.
